reading.body:
Stream Data Centers Houston occupies a facility in The Woodlands with no published power specification available from the operator's own page. The operator, Stream Data Centers, was acquired by Apollo funds with completion on November 3, 2025, and operates more than 20 campuses nationally with a 4 plus gigawatt development pipeline and reported leasing of more than 90 percent of capacity to Fortune 100 customers. This specific campus, internally coded IAHA, has no disclosed IT load or capacity figure from which to estimate racks or accelerators.

Texas has 18 facilities with published megawatt figures across 133 mapped data center locations in the state, totaling 468.41 MW of disclosed capacity. This campus does not appear in that published ranking, meaning either its capacity remains undisclosed or falls below the smallest published figure in the state. Without published power specifications, its rank and share of Texas capacity cannot be determined.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the absence of a published power figure is decisive. The operator's national scale and acquisition by a major alternative-asset fund suggest serious capital backing, but no public specification exists to evaluate this facility's contribution to grid-constrained AI compute capacity. Any assessment of its relevance requires either a direct disclosure from Stream Data Centers or independent measurement.
